title: J.A.R.V.I.S — Voice CLI for Gemini
description: Voice-first layer over the Gemini CLI: summarises output conversationally and lets you interrupt mid-sentence
longDescription: A hands-free co-pilot for CLI-based LLMs. Instead of reading walls of code aloud, every model response passes through a summarisation prompt before hitting the TTS engine. Built on hexagonal architecture so local (faster-whisper, Piper) and remote (OpenAI, ElevenLabs) engines are interchangeable via config — the core FSM never knows which one is running.

data.label: Microphone
data.details: Captured with sounddevice/PyAudio on a dedicated listener thread that never blocks, so speech can be detected even while the assistant is talking.

data.label: VAD Listener
data.description: Voice Activity Detection — the barge-in trigger
data.details: Silero VAD running on its own thread. Silence means 'you finished talking' and flushes the buffer to STT. Speech detected while the FSM is in SPEAKING raises INTERRUPT_SIGNAL, which cancels the audio player mid-sentence and drops back to LISTENING. This is the hardest engineering problem in the project: you cannot block a thread playing audio and expect it to listen at the same time.

data.label: Core FSM
data.description: IDLE → LISTENING → THINKING → SUMMARIZING → SPEAKING → WAITING_APPROVAL
data.details: The finite state machine is the only place that knows the conversation flow. WAITING_APPROVAL is a blocking state: anything that writes a file or runs a shell command stops here until the user approves by voice. The core depends on ports only — swapping ElevenLabs for Piper changes zero lines of FSM code.

data.label: ISpeechRecognizer
data.details: Strategy pattern. LocalWhisperAdapter runs faster-whisper (CTranslate2) on CPU or GPU; OpenAIWhisperAdapter calls the hosted API. Selected by config.yaml or environment variable at startup.

data.label: Gemini Proxy
data.description: Intercepts raw CLI output before it reaches the screen
data.details: Captures the Gemini CLI's final answer and routes it through a summariser prompt: raw output → conversational output → TTS. The rule is absolute — raw code blocks are never spoken. 'I generated the Python script using pandas. Run it, or save it to a file?' instead of dictating 40 lines of source.

data.label: ITextToSpeech
data.details: LocalPiperAdapter uses Piper (ONNX) for low-latency offline synthesis; ElevenLabsAdapter streams over WebSocket. Both must honour a cancellation signal so barge-in works regardless of which is active.

data.label: Interruptible Player
data.description: Audio output thread that accepts cancellation
data.details: Buffers and plays synthesized speech. On INTERRUPT_SIGNAL it flushes the output buffer immediately rather than finishing the current utterance — the difference between an assistant that feels responsive and one that talks over you.

keyFeatures.title: It never reads code aloud
keyFeatures.description: Every model response passes through a summariser prompt before reaching TTS. You hear 'I generated the script using pandas — run it or save it?' instead of forty dictated lines of source.

keyFeatures.title: Barge-in that actually interrupts
keyFeatures.description: A VAD listener runs on its own thread. Speech detected while the assistant is talking raises INTERRUPT_SIGNAL, which flushes the audio buffer mid-sentence instead of finishing the utterance.

keyFeatures.title: Engines are swappable by config
keyFeatures.description: Ports and adapters: local faster-whisper and Piper, or remote OpenAI and ElevenLabs. Switching costs a config line and zero changes to the state machine.

keyFeatures.title: Destructive actions block on approval
keyFeatures.description: Anything that writes a file or runs a shell command parks in WAITING_APPROVAL until you confirm by voice.
